title: Quantization-tailored Attention Planarizer and Zero-copy Dequant Elision
creator: Aarti Mehta
description: Background: Short decode latency is being dominated by repeated dequant (INT8/FP8 -> FP16/FP32) copies and layout conversions inside our attention microkernels. For streaming and low-token workloads the dequant cost is often larger than the compute cost of the attention kernel itself. Goal: implement an attention 'planarizer' and accompanying scheduler/kind-adapter that (1) enables zero-copy dequant views for packed head layouts, (2) amortizes dequant work during prefill/path-prefetch, and (3) integrates a cost model into kernel selection so the runtime prefers mixed-precision kernels only when they reduce end-to-end latency and memory pressure.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end P95 decode latency reduction >= 12% on short-seq workloads (<=64 tokens) compared to baseline mixed-precision path
No model quality regressions (logprob / eval prompts) > 0.2% on benchmark suite v2
Automated perf microbench in CI with deterministic outputs and threshold guards
Feature gated behind runtime flag 'quant.planarizer' and can be toggled at route level

decisions: Keep dequant metadata in KV cache header so repeated decodes avoid recomputing per-head scale/bias maps
Planarization layout will be head-major contiguous with 128B alignment to match microkernel vector lanes
Use a hybrid cost model: static kernel peak throughput + dynamic measurements of recent dequant time per node
Feature will be opt-in via 'quant.planarizer' flag initially and per-tenant route override supported
technical_notes: Zero-copy approach: create read-only FP16/FP32 views that map into INT8/FP8 backing buffer using on-device reinterpretation where supported (NVIDIA CUDA 12 feature) or a light-weight on-GPU reinterpret kernel for older stacks

Planarizer will pack attention QKV heads into a contiguous plane during prefill with head-order chosen to minimize stride for the chosen microkernel (microkernel expects [H,SEQ,DK] contiguous), reducing strided loads during decode
To avoid additional writes during prefill, we will use an ephemeral scratch allocator that writes packed planes once and then drops the original layout lazily after TTL expires

Scheduler will attach a 'dequant credit' to requests: small requests may consume dequant credits from prefill amortization allowing zero dequant in decode path; large requests will fall back to dequant-on-demand
Kernel adapter exposes an interface: selectKernel(model, layer, headLayout, seqLen, recentMetricSnapshot) -> {kernelId, requiresDequant, estimatedCostMs}
Quant metadata schema: per-layer {scale_table_version, head_scales_hash, format: INT8/FP8, preferred_kernel_ids}
We will instrument through perf counters and add an export to existing Console dashboards (tokens/sec, dequant-time, kernel-fallback-rate)
risks: Compatibility: Some GPUs and drivers may not support the zero-copy reinterpret primitives; fallbacks must be correct and not slower
Memory pressure: planarization duplicates buffers transiently, risk of OOM on large-batch prefill; mitigated by TTL + scratch allocator and memory accounting
Correctness risk: FP8 cast differences could change logits slightly, need careful QA against evaluation suite
Scheduler complexity: reordering prefill might increase tail latency for some multi-tenant patterns if not carefully throttled
qa_plan: Unit tests for kernel adapter selection logic with mocked cost model
Deterministic microbench runs across representative model sizes (Llama-2-7B, Llama-2-70B-small-local config)
Regression eval suite with 2k prompt pairs measuring logprob / token-level deltas
A/B canary traffic with quality monitoring and automated rollback if quality delta > 0.5%
Memory/oom fuzzing on canary cluster with stress harness (owner: SRE)
rollout_plan: Mergeto-canary: enable 'quant.planarizer' in dedicated-canary cluster for 10% routes (2 days smoke)
Shadow run: replicate production traffic to canary for 48 hours and compare latencies and correctness metrics
Canary promote: 25% of routes for 7 days, monitor p95/p99 and kernel_fallback_rate
GA gate: after 14-day telemetry review and signoff from perf + SRE + PM
Rollback knob: global disable flag + per-route override + rollback script in runbook
